title: For regular finitely summable spectral triples with invertible weight, holomorphic dimension-spectrum control, bounded pole multiplicity and negative-integer spectrum stability, the finite-part zeta trace vanishes on commutators whose summed orders avoid the negative dimension spectrum
author: Sylvie Paycha
work: A Canonical Trace Associated with Certain Spectral Triples
source_version: Official SIGMA 6 (2010) article 077, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2010.077; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

difficulty_reason: Ordinary trace cyclicity does not survive finite-part regularization: commutators create higher residue defects. The author first constructs meromorphic traces of holomorphic abstract operator families, tracks their order and logarithmic derivatives, and expresses every defect through a finite higher-residue expansion. Dimension-spectrum translation stability then forces all relevant residue terms to vanish at admissible orders, producing the canonical commutator property without assuming a classical manifold calculus.

proof_review.note: Read complete regular spectral triple, smooth domain, summability and abstract order/log-polyhomogeneous definitions3-7; full strengthened holomorphic-family assumption(H) and Definition5 on8-9; pole order(Dk), spectrum translation(T) and full meromorphic-family proof Proposition3 on9-10; full scaled higher-residue expansion Theorem1 on11; complete cyclic analytic continuation/logarithmic commutator defect Proposition5 on13-14; and full holomorphy off negative spectrum Lemma2 and Proposition7 closure14-15. Select only the canonical finite-part commutator property at summed order a+b outside -Sd, for the original H/Dk/T framework. Standard Higson/Connes-Moscovici abstract pseudodifferential commutator expansions are precisely cited foundations. Actual new holomorphic-family and residue-defect arguments are written. No unconditional arbitrary spectral-triple theorem, trace uniqueness, classical odd-class uniqueness result, or perturbation family counted. The formal zero-order perturbation Proposition6 is not selected. Theorem1 introductory proof sentence prints a minus exponent for the constant-order Taylor family, while its displayed expansion and every derivative use the plus exponent; retain original source and this bounded prose warning, without altering formula bytes. The intermediate derivative sentence on14 prints L(A) without an n-th iterate although the immediately following displayed defect expansion uses L^n(B). Both source forms are retained; no coefficient or derivative formula is repaired. Exact selected statement and terminal proof pages rendered and visually inspected; physical headers/native ZIP members and source/license hashes checked. No independent mathematical reproof.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Proposition7 for a regular finitely summable spectral triple with invariant smooth domain and invertible absolute D, Fréchet algebra and abstract holomorphic families as Definition5, assumption(H) meromorphic holomorphic-family trace continuation to the fixed discrete spectrum Sd, finite pole multiplicity bound k+1 (Dk), and Sd-N subset Sd (T). Define tau_minus1(A)=finitePart_{z=0}Tr(A absoluteD^{-z}). For original abstract pseudodifferential A,B of complex orders a,b with a+b outside -Sd, tau_minus1([A,B])=0. Linear combinations are interpreted in the source footnote8 sense. No arbitrary spectral triple, trace uniqueness or zero-order perturbation assertion.
